from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs');p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages):
 text=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 texts.append(f'\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n'+text)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(texts))
print('\\n'.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

s=Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()
start=s.index('===== PAGE 4 =====')
end=s.index('===== PAGE 9 =====')
print(s[start:end])

print(s[s.index('===== PAGE 9 ====='):])

 print({'K':k,'squared_loss_change':1,'Eq11_RHS':round(first+correct_second,6),'Eq10_RHS_if_intermediate_outputs_follow_App8':round(first+eq10_second,6)})
PY"

strengths: QuEST addresses an important practical problem: low-bit diffusion quantization with affordable adaptation. Selectively tuning temporal and attention-related layers, together with activation scales, provides a useful alternative to full finetuning and LoRA. The reported trainable fraction is below 7% for LDM-4.

The empirical coverage is substantial, spanning unconditional, class-conditional, and text-to-image generation, with additional CIFAR10 results. At W4A4, QuEST improves LSUN-Bedrooms FID from EfficientDM’s 10.60 to 5.64 and LSUN-Churches FID from 14.34 to 11.76 (Table 3). These are meaningful gains in settings where several PTQ baselines fail.

The component studies provide useful evidence. Table 6 improves Bedrooms FID from 6.95 to 4.41 with temporal alignment and then to 3.26 with critical-module alignment. Table 7 supports combining local and global supervision. The activation histograms, sensitivity analysis, and token-corruption examples help motivate the approach.

The manuscript is generally well organized and appropriately cites the principal methods, datasets, and pretrained models. It provides key optimization and sampling settings, a code link, and a relevant discussion of potential effects on watermarking and safety checking.
weaknesses: The theoretical analysis needs correction, beyond its acknowledged status as heuristic motivation. Equation (11) uses the stepwise quadratic term involving epsilon, whereas Equation (10) substitutes cumulative activation residuals without justification. Furthermore, for MSE directly on the final activation, the second-order Taylor expansion is exact regardless of perturbation magnitude; an intermediate-feature interpretation requires additional assumptions. These issues weaken the theoretical explanation without directly invalidating the empirical method.

The central efficiency comparison is difficult to interpret consistently. Table 6 reports 15.25 GPU-hours and FID 3.26 for W4A8 QuEST, while Table 8 reports 0.45 hours and FID 3.82 on LDM-4 without clearly explaining the accounting or configuration differences. Calibration generation, quantization initialization, and finetuning costs should be separated and compared consistently. Actual low-bit inference latency and peak inference memory are also unmeasured, limiting the deployment claims.

EfficientDM baseline validation needs more explanation. Table 3 reports generation failure at W8A8 on both LSUN datasets despite successful W4A4 generation; on Bedrooms, its W4A8 FID is also substantially worse than W4A4. These unexplained outcomes reduce confidence in the magnitude of the claimed advantage. Exact quantizer granularity, selected-module lists, batch sizes, and per-stage training schedules are insufficiently specified for reproduction from the manuscript.

The originality lies mainly in the selection and sequencing of trainable modules, since temporal preservation and teacher-based reconstruction build on cited approaches. The ablations do not fully isolate this contribution: adding TLA and CMA also increases the trainable parameter budget, and there are no comparisons against alternative subsets with matched budgets or joint/reversed training orders.

Text-to-image evaluation relies exclusively on CLIP Score, which does not adequately establish image fidelity or diversity. Figure 8 shows visible W4A4 degradation, and Table 4 reports a substantial ImageNet IS reduction from 364.73 to 202.45 despite improved FID. Stronger perceptual and distributional evaluation would better characterize the remaining quality tradeoff. Uncertainty estimates would also help interpret small improvements at higher precisions.
